description_full: DPC Dash Ltd, together with its subsidiaries, operates a chain of fast-food restaurants in the People's Republic of China. It offers fast-food products, such as pizza, and beverages. In addition, the company engages in restaurant management, dough production, and provides warehousing services. DPC Dash Ltd was formerly known as Dash Brands Ltd and changed its name to DPC Dash Ltd in September 2021. The company was incorporated in 2008 and is headquartered in Shanghai, China.

Stock-based compensation of $657 per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 16× revenue per employee (reasonable relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: DPC DASH LTD is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $553M market cap on $808M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +36% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +3.6pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 1% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 43%.

The business throws off $58M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 6.29× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -13.3% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 3.3×.

Net dilution runs at 0.4% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 39% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
